# If you re-priced an H100 SXM plan around last week’s increase, it is gone: Crusoe’s published H100 read $4.50 in our October 18, 2026 catalog and $3.90 again in our October 26, … | Bobby Clay · LinkedIn · 2026-10-28T00:00:00+00:00

**Bobby Clay**.

---

If you re-priced an H100 SXM plan around last week’s increase, it is gone: Crusoe’s published H100 read $4.50 in our October 18, 2026 catalog and $3.90 again in our October 26, 2026 catalog.

Its H200 did the same, from $5.40 to $4.29 across the same two catalogs. Both match our October 11, 2026 catalog, and Crusoe again holds the lowest published H100 SXM across the nine providers we track, under Lambda’s $3.99 in the same October 26, 2026 catalog.

Ornn’s Compute Price Index (OCPI), a third-party index of traded prices rather than quoted or listed ones, rose in three of four families between October 19 and October 26, 2026. B200 reached $9.76 on October 26, 2026, up from $8.41 on October 19, 2026, while the lowest published B200 across those nine held at $6.69 in our October 26, 2026 catalog.

A published rate that moves up and back between captures is a rate to date, not a rate to anchor to.

Nine providers, every figure dated.

results.title: Are 200 Neoclouds About to Collapse? Our Data Says No
results.author: Chad Everett Harris
highlights:
GPU cloud list-price index, Sep 11 to Oct 26+6.1% SAVRN Index, 117 same-item list prices 2 

GPU prices that rose vs. fell, same period 43 vs. 3 182 prices incl. spot and reserved 3 

Verda H100 on-demand, per GPU-hour$3.25 → $4.56+40% in six weeks 3 

H100 standard on-demand range$1.99–$12.29 31 offers, median $4.09 3

...

The SAVRN Index tracks 229 GPU prices from 27 providers across 10 GPU types. 9 In addition, across all four markets we follow, it holds 797 prices from 55 providers. 10 For the GPU cloud market, we publish a same-item index of list prices. Because only items priced on both days count, a new product launch or an expiring discount cannot move it. 2 

Since September 11, that index has risen 6.1%. 2 

Figure 1. The same 117 published GPU prices, checked every day since September 11, rose 6.1%. Only prices checked on both days count, so launches and expiring discounts cannot move the index. Chart: SAVRN.

Looking wider, we also followed every GPU price we could from mid-September through late October, including spot, serverless and reserved prices. Of 182 such prices, 43 rose while only 3 fell. 3 

The increases were not random. In particular, short-term and flexible prices moved first: spot, serverless, capacity blocks and monthly reservations. By contrast, one-year and three-year reserved prices did not move. That pattern is what you would expect if buyers who need capacity now are bidding for it.

One seller makes the point clearly, since Verda reprices its GPUs every few days. Its H100 on-demand price rose from $3.25 an hour on September 11 to $4.56 on October 25, an increase of 40%. 3 In fact, all 23 of the Verda prices we track went up.

Figure 2. Verda's published H100 on-demand price stepped up ten times in six weeks, with no cuts. Chart: SAVRN.

Others moved too, although less sharply. For example, Runpod’s tracked prices rose a median of about 14%. AWS capacity blocks rose a median of 7.5%, while individual Nebius and Crusoe prices rose 20% and 15%. 3 Meanwhile, Azure, Google, CoreWeave and Lambda left their tracked prices unchanged.

Six weeks is a short record, and I want to be plain about that. Our list prices do not show discounts, utilization or what any provider actually collects. Still, they are enough to reject the story that GPU prices are collapsing. Outside data points the same way. For example, SemiAnalysis reported that one-year H100 rental contract prices rose almost 40%, from $1.70 an hour in October 2025 to $2.35 by March 2026. 11 

## The same H100, from $1.99 to $12.29

Here is the number that made me rethink this market. Our latest check found 31 standard on-demand prices for an NVIDIA H100. 3 The cheapest was $1.99 an hour, while the most expensive was $12.29. The median was $4.09. Our GPU page, which also counts calendar-mode and serverless rates, shows 38 on-demand prices with a typical price of $4.35. 9 

Figure 3. Same chip, same week: 31 standard on-demand offers. Most GPU clouds charge $2 to $5 an hour; Azure, Google and Oracle list $10 to $12.29. Chart: SAVRN.

...

Our latest check found 31 standard on-demand H100 prices, from $1.99 to $12.29 per GPU-hour, with a median of $4.09. The hyperscalers’ standard on-demand rates ran $10.00 to $12.29.

results.title: GPU cloud pricing: the list price is not the price | Casitel
highlights:
H100 rate cards ran from $1.99 to $9.80 a GPU-hour on 8 October 2026. Large buyers rarely pay them. How GPU deals close, and how to benchmark a quote.

C Compute · H100 list prices, per GPU-hour Rate cards read 8 October 2026

$3.90 median H100 list price across nine GPU clouds, Casitel OS, 3 November 2026

Range of published on-demand rates Median $3.90 $1.99$9.80

Each provider's own pricing page, read 8 October 2026. Not executed prices.

Every GPU cloud publishes a rate card. Few large buyers pay it. The rate card is where the negotiation starts, not where it ends.

## What the rate cards say

On 8 October 2026 the published on-demand rate for one Nvidia H100 ran from $1.99 to $9.80 an hour, across the providers that state a price per GPU.

Provider Published H100 rate What the rate covers

Voltage Park$1.99 From, bare metal

RunPod$1.99 From, secure cloud

GMI Cloud$2.60 From

Hyperstack$3.20 H100 SXM

Jarvislabs$3.49 H100 SXM

DataCrunch$3.85 H100 SXM5

Nebius$3.85 HGX H100

Crusoe$3.90 HGX H100

Lambda$3.99 H100 SXM, 8 GPUs

Together AI$3.99 HGX H100

Paperspace$5.95 H100

Fireworks AI$8.00 Dedicated H100

Google Cloud$9.80 Vertex AI H100

Each rate is the provider's own published figure, read from its pricing page on 8 October 2026. A rate marked "from" is the lowest tier on the page. Casitel OS reads these rate cards every day: on 3 November 2026 the median H100 list price across nine GPU clouds was $3.90 an hour.

...

A list price is for one GPU, today, with no commitment. A large deal changes every one of those terms.

- Term. A commitment of one year or more is priced below on-demand. DigitalOcean, for example, publishes $3.26 a GPU-hour for an H100 on a 12-month reservation.
- Volume. A cluster of thousands of GPUs is a different product from a single instance. The seller fills a whole hall at once.
- Payment. A deposit or prepayment buys a lower rate. It also moves risk from the seller to the buyer.
- Start date and place. Capacity that is live today costs more than capacity that goes live next year. A region with spare power costs less than one without.
- What is in the hour. Fast networking between GPUs, storage, support and data transfer are priced in some quotes and added on in others.

results.title: Nebius says AI computing prices are rising despite neocloud debt fears
results.author: Arjun Kharpal
highlights:
Chase Lochmiller, CEO of Crusoe, an Nvidia-backed AI company that is building data centers, was also bullish on pricing, saying the company was seeing rising prices for GPUs, including older Nvidia chips.

"We're seeing higher pricing today for A100s than we saw in 2020 or 2021. We're seeing higher pricing for H100s than what we saw when they were first deployed in 2023," Lochmiller said.

"There's tremendous demand and a lot of it is because the underlying model capabilities have gotten so much more advanced that people are just creating so much more value out of the compute infrastructure."

The comments come amid an investor debate over how quickly Nvidia's GPUs lose their economic value as more powerful chips enter the market.

The ability to continue renting out older chips at attractive prices is crucial to AI infrastructure companies that need to recover their investments and generate profits, while spending billions on GPUs.

Lochmiller's comments suggest that, at least for Crusoe, older generations of Nvidia chips are commanding higher rental prices than when they were first deployed, potentially strengthening the economics of its AI cloud business.

results.title: H100 price per hour across 7 clouds (Oct 26, 2026) | joulemath
highlights:
# What an H100 hour costs across 7 clouds (Oct 26, 2026)

How much is one H100 hour this week? We checked 7 public price lists and one trade index on October 26, 2026. Fixed on-demand prices run from $2.69 to $6.16 per GPU-hour. The index of real trades sits at $3.03.

## H100 SXM, per GPU per hour

| Where | Price | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| RunPod Community | $2.69 | 1 GPU, on-demand. Secure Cloud is $3.99. |
| Ornn OCPI-H100 | $3.03 | Index of executed rental trades, page updated Oct 25, 20:00 UTC |
| Massed Compute | $3.14 | 1x H100 SXM5, on-demand |
| Vast.ai median (affiliate) | $3.20 | Marketplace, 4 single-GPU offers: $1.93 low, $9.10 high |
| Together AI | $3.99 | GPU clusters, on-demand. $3.19 if reserved 181+ days. |
| Lambda | $4.29 | 1 GPU. $3.99 per GPU on an 8x instance. Plus tax. |
| Nebius | $4.50 | HGX H100, on-demand |
| CoreWeave | $6.16 | 8-GPU HGX H100 at $49.24/hr, divided by 8 (our math) |

All pages read October 26, 2026, about 09:00 to 10:00 CET. Vast numbers come from its public offer search (console.vast.ai/api/v0/bundles) at 09:06 CET: rentable, on-demand, exactly one H100 SXM. Four offers is a tiny sample, so the median can jump hour to hour. RunPod's page still says "Updated October 8, 2026".

## What jumps out

- More than 2x spread. $2.69 at the low fixed price, $6.16 at the high one. Same chip, different packaging: single GPU vs 8-GPU boxes, support, network, contract terms.
- Commitment cuts the price. Together lists $3.99 on demand and $3.19 for 181+ days. Lambda's 8x box is $0.30 per GPU-hour cheaper than its single GPU.
- The trade index is in the middle. Ornn's $3.03 is up 6.32% over one month, per Ornn.
- Newer chips are moving faster. On the same Ornn page, H200 is $6.30 (+24.02% in a month) and B200 is $9.70 (+20.65%).
